label: EXECUTED
design: docs/proposals/native-oracle.md, slice 4 (floats; aggregates and sums in oracle_aggregates_evidence.json)

areas.area: float.add, float.sub, float.mul, float.div in binary32 and binary64
areas.corpus: tests/test_native_oracle.py test_both_oracles_agree_on_floats: 14 x 14 values per operation and width (zeros, normals, subnormals, the largest finite values, infinities, NaN, 12 seeded random values)

areas.area: float.compare, all six predicates, both widths
areas.corpus: the same test: 7 pairs, NaN among them
the same test: 31 values each way (rounding, overflow, subnormal results)

areas.area: uint.to.float, sint.to.float from bits<8>, bits<32>, bits<64>
areas.corpus: the same test: the edge integers of each width into both float widths

areas.area: float.to.uint.trunc, float.to.sint.trunc to bits<8>, bits<32>, bits<64>, with the float-conversion trap
areas.corpus: the same test: 18 values per width pair, 104 of all float cases trap

areas.area: test_xax_general_language's float program, constant, compare and conversions
areas.corpus: tests/test_xax_general_language.py, now through oracle_execute: the native oracle gives the test's literal expected values (not a comparison with the Python executor)

agreement_rule: results are compared as IEEE bits; any two NaNs agree (the oracle returns the canonical quiet NaN, the Python executor the host's NaN)
method: integer arithmetic only, no XAX float operation: XAX has no bits-to-float reinterpretation (a pointer.cast between element types is rejected, XAX.MEMORY.POINTER_CAST, and a checked load is always bits); round to nearest, ties to even
also: the earlier corpora still agree (test_native_oracle 6,159 subtests on Windows; 10,084 subtests with the oracle-backed tests on Linux)

native.store: compiler/bootstrap/oracle/xax_oracle.xax (oracle, driver and the four slice-4 batches)
native.built_by: the pinned Windows seed (Windows 11) and the pinned Linux seed (WSL 2, XAX_REQUIRE_NATIVE=1); both make the same stores

host_nonsemantic: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 x86-64, Python 3.12.10; WSL 2 Linux x86-64, Python 3.12.3
